subject.title: Feature request: api.callGatewayMethod() for inter-plugin communication

question: Should OpenClaw expose plugin-to-plugin Gateway method calls to ordinary external plugins, and if yes what authorization and API shape should make that safe?
rationale: Current code proves the runtime can dispatch Gateway methods for trusted plugins, but extending that to arbitrary external plugins changes the public Plugin SDK and plugin isolation boundary.

options.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
options.body: Expose only approved plugin-owned methods or typed service capabilities with caller attribution, docs, and contract tests.

options.title: Keep the trusted-only surface
options.body: Treat current `api.runtime.gateway.request` as the supported boundary and decline ordinary external plugin-to-plugin Gateway calls.

options.title: Allow raw method dispatch
options.body: Expose a generic method-string caller and explicitly accept the larger compatibility and security surface.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow authorized contract
recommendation.body: Expose only approved plugin-owned methods or typed service capabilities with caller attribution, docs, and contract tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the current trusted-plugin Gateway request surface and is the strongest available routing owner for the SDK/security boundary decision.
